subject: Howto access elements in a vector of covariance matrices?

messages.author: 2300d3769456dbe6
messages.subject: Howto access elements in a vector of covariance matrices?
parts:
Dear user list,

I am working with multidimensional data and hereto created the following data types:

corr_matrix[6] Omega_s[Nstudies]; //6x6 correlation matrix for 15 studies
vector<lower=0>[6] sigma_s[Nstudies]; //6 variance components for 15 studies

My question is how I can access individual entries from Omega_s and sigma_s, e.g. to create the study-specific covariance matrices:

cov_matrix[6] Sigma_s[Nstudies];
   for (j in 1:Nstudies) { //is this loop needed?
      for (r in 1:6) {
         for (c in 1:6) {
            // the following statement needs to be implemented for each study
            //(Sigma_s[r,c]) <- (sigma_s[r]) * (sigma_s[c]) * (Omega_s[r,c]); //vectorized approach? does not work
            //(Sigma_s[r,c])[j] <- (sigma_s[r])[j] * (sigma_s[c])[j] * (Omega_s[r,c])[j]; //does not work either
         }
      }
   }

An alternative option is to directly define 

cov_matrix[6] Sigma_s[Nstudies];

and to have Sigma_s follow an inverse Wishart distribution. HOwever, this approach is less recommended.

THanks for your help!

Thomas

My question is how I can access individual entries from Omega_s and sigma_s, e.g. to create the study-specific covariance matrices:

Omega_s[1][2,3] will access the element in the second row and third column of the first correlation matrix and so on.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Howto access elements in a vector of covariance matrices?

And so should Omega_s[1,2,3] and Omega_s[1][2][3]. The last
one's not very efficient, though. There's a chapter on the manual
right up front about indexing and arrays vs. vectors and matrices
and how to index them.

- Bob
